summary: The type check is inverted: it now raises TypeError for every str header value and lets None through to .encode().

findings.explanation: `if isinstance(value, str): raise TypeError` rejects all normal string header values, breaking essentially all requests, while None still falls through to `value.encode` and raises AttributeError, so the new test fails.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `if not isinstance(value, str):` raise TypeError.
